The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the
Recreation Commission with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Monday of every month at 6:00 p.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the Community Services Department via email at
KShigenaga@SanMarinoCA.gov or by phone at (626) 300­0791 at least 48 hours prior to the
meeting.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City will
do its best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

How to view or listen to the meeting from home:
Visit www.SanMarinoCA.gov/Zoom.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the Recreation

BACKGROUND

The Community Services Director and Recreation Manager provide a monthly
report to the Recreation Commission. It provides relevant administrative,
operational, and financial updates, in addition to upcoming events, marketing
and communication efforts, and customer feedback.

DISCUSSION

  positions
  • Part-time position recruitments currently underway include:

FY 2024-25 Budget Update
At the April 26 City Council meeting, the City Manager and department heads
presented proposed operating budgets for the upcoming fiscal year. The city-
wide operating budget was presented with a $1.3MM shortfall with staff

  PAGE 11 of 30
 seeking guidance from Council on strategic areas to decrease to bring the
budget into balance. Subsequently, departments were asked to revisit their
budget submissions and submit generous decreases for the City Manager’s
review. Recreation staff found approximately $20K in reductions, which do not
impact personnel nor program service delivery. Final adoption of the City’s FY
2024-25 Operating Budget will take place at the Council meeting on Friday,
May 31 at 8:30 AM.

Join Us for Memorial Day Service at Lacy Park
We invite you to attend this year’s Memorial Day Service on Monday, May 27
beginning at 9 AM. It’s truly a humbling and moving experience. Dedicated on
November 11, 2007, San Marino’s War Memorial is a stunning tribute to our
fallen soldiers. The Memorial includes seven engraved granite panels, a statue
of a kneeling soldier, a service recognition, an attractive plaza-like setting,
beautiful landscaping, and a Veterans’ Walk. The Veterans’ Walk allows family
and friends to order name engravings to recognize loved ones who served in
the Armed Forces. Their names are etched in the walk curving around the
Memorial.

Operational Staff Briefings
  All City Track & Field Meet
  The 49th annual All City Track & Field Meet was held on Friday, March
  15 at San Marino High School. Welcoming 260 participants born
  between 2009 and 2017, the event featured an array of competitions
  including team relays, 50 / 100 / 200 / 400 / 1600-meter races, and
  long jump and softball throw field events. Athletes that came in 1st and
  2nd place in each event will move on to the San Gabriel Valley Track &
  Field Championships hosted by the City of Glendora.

  During the meet, concession stands were open and managed by San
  Marino High School’s Girls’ Basketball Team. There was a 20-minute
  delay during the event due to safety concerns following nearby lightning
  strikes. The Department would like to thank San Marino Community
  Athletics Association (SMCAA) for their continued monetary support.

  PAGE 13 of 30
 The Great San Marino Egg Hunt
Due to the rainy weather on March 30, the Great San Marino Egg Hunt
pivoted from the traditional event at Lacy Park to a drive through
experience at the Community Center. 5,400 candy and toy filled eggs
along with two crafts were handed out to 160 children. The drive
through experience led cars along a path decorated with inflatables,
spring backdrops, and the Easter Bunny. Families unable to make it to
the drive through were given the option to pick up a DIY egg hunt kit at
the Community Center. A total of 293 kits containing 9,962 eggs were
picked up.

Earth Day Kite Making Class
On April 5, over 50 people participated in an Earth Day Kite Making Class
at Lacy Park. Families were given kits containing sticks, paper, glue,
crayons, and markers to make their own custom kites. Staff
demonstrated how to assemble, decorate, and fly their kites in the windy
afternoon. Families enjoyed spending quality time together flying their
kites.

Spring Break Camp
Running April 8 through 12 from 9 AM to 4 PM at the Stoneman Building,
the Recreation Division’s Spring Break Camp was a success! 17
participants were provided an immersive and fun spring break
experience. Children played games, participated in sports, and made
arts & crafts. Many parents were pleased with the childcare option
offered to them.

Senior Trip: Dodger Game
On April 17, a sold-out excursion to Dodger Stadium left San Marino to
watch the “Boys in Blue” take on the Washington Nationals. Despite the
Dodgers losing the game, 19 participants enjoyed a beautiful day at the
stadium watching the game and enjoying snacks from the concession
stands.

Nature Series: Spring Tree Walk
On April 19, the City’s Urban Forester, Lora Hall, led a stroll around Lacy
Park informing 20 participants on trees currently blooming and the
unique features or history behind them.

ROCK LACY! Battle of the Youth Rock Bands
The inaugural ROCK LACY! Battle of the Youth Rock Bands that took
place on April 20 was a rockin’ success! Five enthusiastic youth bands
brought the park to life directly following the San Marino Firefighters
Association Pancake Breakfast. The talented young rockstars performed

  PAGE 14 of 30
   their best songs to a crowd of over 600 spectators. The competition was
  strong as each band was trying to earn audience votes, as they vied for
  prizes and a chance to perform at the City’s 4th of July Celebration. In
  the end, the winning band was “WANTED 5,” a group composed of very
  impressive 10 to 14-year-old musicians!

  In addition to the musical performances, there were 3 food trucks, 8
  vendors leading family activities, and free train rides around the Rose
  Arbor. A huge thank you to the local sponsor, San Marino Music Center,
  who provided a tremendous amount of technical and promotional
  support. All bands and their families shared that they had a blast
  participating and playing to the live audience, and that they plan to
  compete again next year.

  Lil’ Learners Open House
  On April 24, the Department hosted an Open House for Lil' Learners.
  Families of current students and those considering enrollment were
  invited to tour the facility. The event provided an opportunity for families
  to explore two classrooms, admire their child's ongoing projects,
  interact with staff, and seek clarification on any questions they had.
  Each classroom had its own unique theme; one showcased an art exhibit
  and the other adorned with a jungle motif. A total of 85 people attended
  the event.

BACKGROUND

The Department’s FY 2023-24 Priority Initiative, Rebuild a Sense of
Community, includes a multicultural summer concert to complement the
existing more traditional Summer Sunset Concert Series. The first ever
multicultural concert occurred last summer (August 2023). Staff is beginning
to plan the next one taking place on August 16. Like last year, the concert will
include music from other countries, culturally-diverse entertainment, food
trucks, and a variety of community outreach booths for our community
partners.

DISCUSSION

Today, staff seeks direction from the Commission on the selection of one (1)
cultural performance and one (1) musical genre. As a reminder, the concert
is family-oriented.

Concert Timeline
  • 5:30 PM  Event Begins / Announcements / Introductions
  • 5:45 PM  Cultural Performance: TBD by Commission (30 minutes)
  • 6:15 PM  Band Set-up

  PAGE 18 of 30
   •  6:45 PM  Musical Performance #1: Diego Qin Dai (Chinese Rock &
  Roll)
  •  7:15 PM  Musical Performance #2: TBD by Commission (1.5 hours)
  •  8:45 PM  Event Ends

Event Format
Below is a diverse list of cultural performances and music genres.

Cultural Performance Options:
  • Brazilian Folkloric
  • North Indian Classical Dance
  • West African Dance Ensemble
  • Peruvian Ensemble
  • Philippine Folk Arts / Dance
  • Korean Classical Music and Dance
  • Melody of China
  • Fandango
  • Japanese Drumming
  • American Doo Wop

Genres of Music Options:
  • Mariachi
  • Caribbean Reggae
  • American Rock and Roll
  • Jazz
  • Bluegrass
  • Classical

Note: all entertainment is subject to the availability of the performers / bands.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends the Commission consider the following: Philippine Folk Arts
/ Dance for the cultural performance and Caribbean Reggae as the music
genre, and provide two back-up choices for each. If the Commission concurs
with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

“I move to recommend staff secure Philippine Folk Arts / Dance as the cultural
performance with ____________ and ____________ as back-up choices, and
a Caribbean Reggae band with ____________ and ____________ as back-
up choices for the multicultural concert.”

SUBJECT: UPDATE ON 4TH OF JULY PARADE THEME AND GRAND
  MARSHAL SELECTION PROCESS AND A CALL FOR (2) PARADE

STRATEGIC PLAN CRITICAL SUCCESS FACTORS

Engaged and Connected Residents
Efficient, Responsive, and Effective City Services

BACKGROUND

For several years, the Rotary Club of San Marino produced and managed the
4th of July community parade offered as part of the City’s 4th of July
Independence Day Celebration. Each year, Rotary Club received support from
the City’s Police and Parks and Public Works Departments, who assisted in
supervising the parade route.

In February 2024, the City Council asked staff to submit an assessment and
proposal for the Community Services Department (CSD) to assume parade
management responsibilities beginning with this year’s event. Subsequently,
at the February 23, 2024 City Council meeting, funding was approved during
a mid-year budget request to support parade management operations by CSD.

In March, staff began the planning efforts related to new oversight
responsibilities of the community parade, which is held outside of Lacy Park,
prior to the fireworks show on July 4. The parade has been re-branded to a
“Parade-Palooza – Come Make Some Noise” theme.

In addition to this general update on parade management, staff are seeking
the assistance of (2) Recreation Commissioners to serve on the Parade

  PAGE 20 of 30
 Committee. The role and responsibility of the Parade Committee is outlined
below.

DISCUSSION

In addition to general parade management, staff will oversee the nomination
and selection process for the Parade’s Grand Marshal by way of a Parade
Committee. The Parade Committee’s role and function are outlined below:

Role of the Committee
The Parade Committee’s role is to select the Grand Marshal for the current
year’s parade. The Community Services Director will provide administrative
support to the Committee as the group moves through the judging, selection,
and announcement process.

The Committee shall be made up of the following representatives:
  • (2) Council Liaisons for Community Services Department (CSD)
  • (2) Recreation Commissioners
  • (1) City Manager or Designee

Judging, Selection, and Announcement Process
  1. Deadline for nominations is Friday, May 31, 2024.
  2. Parade Committee Members will receive a physical packet containing all
  Grand Marshal Nominees, including a rater sheet for each, on
  Thursday, June 6.
  3. Rater sheets will be due back to the CSD Director on Thursday, June
  13.
  4. An in-person or virtual (Zoom) Committee meeting will be held the
  week of June 17 (based on members’ availability) to determine final
  Grand Marshal Selection.
  5. On or before Monday, June 24, the winner will be notified by the City
  Manager or Designee.
  6. On Monday, June 24, a press release and photo announcing the winner
  will be sent to the San Marino Tribune, and other local media outlets. In
  addition, the announcement will be posted on the City’s website and
  social media pages.

Grand Marshal Honors and Responsibilities
The Grand Marshal honors and responsibilities include leading the parade,
being announced and honored on the main stage during the program segment
of the 4th of July Celebration (prior to the fireworks), and receiving priority
seating in the main lawn area.

  PAGE 21 of 30
 The Grand Marshal in a parade holds a prestigious position, but its
significance has evolved over time. Let’s delve into the history and
responsibilities associated with this title:

Local Historical Origins:
The concept of a grand marshal in a parade originated in Pasadena,
California during the late 19th century. Initially, parades were more focused
on equestrian units, and each unit had its own marshal. To streamline
coordination, the Tournament of Roses organizers decided to appoint
a grand marshal who would oversee all the marshals, ensuring orderliness
during the parade. The first grand marshal’s role was functional, involving
riding up and down the parade route, keeping both men and horses in line.
However, as the 1920s arrived, the position transitioned into an honorary
role.

The Grand Marshal Nomination Form was made available to the public on the
City’s website on May 3 and is also included as Attachment 1. The City’s
Community Engagement Manager has also submitted a press release to the
San Marino Tribune to advertise that the City’s is seeking nominations for its
Grand Marshal; see Attachment 2.

recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

Parade Committee.”

  PRESS RELEASE:

City of San Marino Assumes Management of 4th of July Parade-Palooza: Calls for Grand
Marshal Nominations

San Marino, CA - May 2, 2024 - The City of San Marino is thrilled to announce its assumption
of management responsibilities for the beloved 4th of July Parade-Palooza. This vibrant
celebration, a cherished tradition in our community, will now be organized by the city itself,
promising the continuation of an event for all to enjoy.

After decades of the 4th of July Parade Management, the San Marino Rotary Club has requested
that the City assume the lead role in the organizing of the parade. While members of Rotary
will still participate in the parade and generously volunteer day-of assistance, the City and Club
have agreed to transfer management responsibilities.

Mayor Steven Huang said, “I’m thrilled that the City Council was able to work with our staff to
find a way to transition this great tradition to the City to keep it going for years to come. I want
to thank the Rotary Club for their many years of stewardship of this wonderful event and for
being wonderful partners to the City and our residents.”

The 4th of July Parade, named Parade-Palooza this year, kicks off in the late afternoon on July
4th at 4:45 PM, just before the dazzling fireworks display. The City invites all community groups,
organizations, and businesses to join us in spreading our special San Marino community spirit
all along the lively parade route. Spanning approximately 1.5 miles along Monterey Road to

  PAGE 27 of 30
 Virginia Road, the parade winds its way through our beautiful neighborhoods, culminating in
the heart of our city at Lacy Park.

To participate, interested parties can access the parade application form and further details
www.SanMarinoCA.gov/Fireworks. The deadline for submissions is June 17 at 12 PM, so don't
miss your chance to be part of this joyous occasion!

In addition to announcing our new management role, the City of San Marino is calling for
nominations for the esteemed position of Grand Marshal for this year's parade. The Grand
Marshal is a symbol of our community's spirit and dedication, representing those who have
made significant contributions to the betterment of San Marino.

Do you know someone deserving of this honor? We encourage all residents to submit their
nominations. The nomination form is available www.SanMarinoCA.gov/Fireworks with a
deadline of May 31.

Join us in celebrating the pride and unity of San Marino this 4th of July Parade-Palooza! For
further information or inquiries, please contact the Recreation Division at (626) 943-2627.
